full_judgment: 25. The present case is an ideal one in which the age old maxim "man may lie but circumstances do not" applies in full force in this case a well-knit-chain of circumstances and some vital facts of grave significance stand out prominently against the prosecution and sharply react in favour of a presumption of innocence of the accused petitioner. It is unfortunate that the learned Courts below totally failed to follow the correct principle of appreciation of the evidence, oral, documentary and circumstantial and to weigh and sift the evidence in accordance with law and the established judicial norms and principles and thereby fell in error in arriving at faulty conclusions on illegal and irrelevant considerations. The impugned judgment, indeed, occasioned failure of justice.
